name: CA-28
label: Safe D

key_factors: Chu holds a massive cash advantage ($3.7M vs $405K)
Prediction markets price Chu near 97% to win
No public polling, but fundamentals uniformly favor the incumbent
model.rationale: A D+14 district, a long-serving incumbent with a roughly nine-to-one cash advantage, and markets pricing Chu near 97% all point the same direction, and no evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: A sharp national backlash against Democrats or an unexpected scandal involving Chu could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Judy Chu, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Los Angeles-area district that leans Democratic by fourteen points. She advanced to the general election with a large financial edge, having raised nearly $1.3 million and reporting $3.7 million on hand, while Republican April Verlato has raised about $450,000. Prediction markets give Chu roughly a 97 percent chance of winning.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, and all three point the same way: a comfortable Democratic margin in the low twenties. Verlato would need a dramatic shift in the national environment or an unforeseen development to make this competitive. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being turnout in a low-profile contest rather than the outcome itself.
